title: Lynx: An Open Source Hallucination Evaluation Model

model.params_source: assumed (the paper gives no decoding parameters for the API baselines; Appendix B.1 states greedy decoding and max_new_tokens = 600 for the self-hosted models, so max_tokens 600 mirrors the paper's own answer budget and temperature 0 is the ANALYSIS_PLAN default)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: the FinanceBench subset of HaluBench (all 1,000 rows, 500 PASS / 500 FAIL)
task.approximation: none; the same zero-shot prompt is used for every model and task (Sec. 4.1), and the FinanceBench column of Table 3 is scored over the whole released subset.

download.note: downloaded only to read the column names, the subset counts and the passage lengths; the runner re-fetches it through the Hub parquet API

prompt.few_shot: none (zero-shot; Sec. 4.1 'We used the same zero-shot prompt for all models and tasks')
prompt.source_location: Appendix A.2 'Evaluation' ('We use the following prompt for instruction fine-tuning as well as for evaluation of models', User Prompt)
prompt.verbatim: full, with two repairs: (a) the extraction's hard line wraps inside sentences were rejoined; (b) the appendix prints the closing JSON example with doubled braces ({{"REASONING": ...}}), which is the Python format-string escape for a single pair of braces, so the single-brace form the model actually received is used here. Nothing else was altered.

output.postprocess: strip, case-insensitive; a reply with no SCORE key counts as incorrect
output.parse_paper: read the JSON key "SCORE" (PASS / FAIL). The regex is used instead of the runner's 'json field SCORE' because the REASONING bullet points frequently contain unescaped quotes and newlines that break a strict json.loads of the whole reply, while the SCORE key itself is unambiguous.

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: fraction of the 1,000 FinanceBench items whose parsed verdict equals the gold label (PASS = faithful, FAIL = hallucinated).
metric.original_location: Table 3, row GPT-4-Turbo, column FinanceBench (the Overall column across all six HaluBench subsets is 85.0%)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run 2026-09-19 (chars/4 input tokens, max_tokens 600 counted as output per call); gpt-4-turbo at $10/$30 per 1M dominates, the inputs are only ~630 tokens per item

notes: The other five columns of Table 3 (HaluEval, RAGTruth, DROP, CovidQA, PubMedQA, and the Overall average) use the very same prompt and the same HaluBench release, so sibling configs are a filter change away; FinanceBench is the cleanest single cell because it is balanced 500/500 and is not one of the subsets the caption flags as containing semantically perturbed samples. || [check 2026-09-19] Hub parquet listing default/test resolves; 14,900 rows with columns id/passage/question/answer/label/source_ds, source_ds == 'FinanceBench' selects exactly 1,000 rows (500 PASS, 500 FAIL, ids unique) and the mean question+passage+answer length is ~630 tokens.
